title: Private deployments: Shadow Traffic constraints (local storage, SIEM export, retention defaults, air-gapped scoring)
creator: Talia Benson
project: Shadow traffic tool for eval metrics
body:
Problem / why
Shadow Traffic in Private deployments (VPC + on-prem) has additional constraints vs Hosted/Dedicated:
- Customer-controlled data plane + storage (often no Redwood-managed object store)
- Strict data residency + retention defaults (regulated / air-gapped environments)
- Centralized export requirements (SIEM) for auditability and incident response
- Scoring options vary: some customers can’t call out to external LLMs for model-graded evals, or can’t run GPU scoring clusters at all

This ticket documents requirements and drives implementation changes so Shadow Traffic behaves predictably in Private deployments and passes security/compliance reviews.

Scope
1) Storage & artifact handling (Private)
- Define where shadow artifacts live (request/response payload refs + scored results):
  - Default: local customer-managed object storage (S3-compatible, GCS, Azure Blob, or on-prem S3 gateway)
  - Alternative: “no artifact persistence” mode that only emits aggregates/metrics (counts/ratios) and drops raw payloads
- Make artifact storage explicit in config and surfaced in Console (Private control plane UI):
  - storage_backend = {customer_object_store | local_filesystem | none}
  - storage_prefix / bucket / region / endpoint
  - encryption mode: SSE-KMS (customer key) / HSM-backed where available
- Ensure prompt/response redaction happens before persistence (no unredacted payloads written anywhere on disk).

2) Retention defaults & knobs (Private)
- Private defaults should be “minimum retention” and “minimum payload”:
  - Default retention for raw artifacts: 0 hours (off) unless explicitly enabled by an admin
  - Default retention for scored results: 7 days (configurable 1–30)
  - Default retention for aggregates/metrics: 30 days (configurable)
  - Default sampling: 0% (off) until explicitly enabled
- Required knobs:
  - retention_raw_hours (0–168)
  - retention_scored_days (1–30)
  - retention_aggregates_days (7–90)
  - allow_payload_storage (true/false) (hard gate)
  - redact_mode = {strict_allowlist | regex_plus_allowlist}
  - max_prompt_chars / max_response_chars (truncate)
- Document “fail-open” behavior: if retention backend is unavailable, shadow path drops artifacts and continues user response.

3) SIEM export (Private)
- Add an export path for *audit and ops* events, not raw prompts:
  - Shadow experiment lifecycle actions (create/edit/disable)
  - Policy changes applied to routes
  - Scoring worker health/lag events (high-level)
  - Redaction configuration changes
- Private needs supported export destinations:
  - Syslog (RFC5424) over TCP/TLS
  - HTTP event collector (Splunk HEC-style)
  - Cloud-native: AWS CloudWatch Logs, Azure Monitor, GCP Cloud Logging (where Private runs in-cloud)
- Define event schema: cardinality-safe, no payload text. Include tenant_id, route_id, experiment_id, rubric_version, timestamps, outcome status codes.
- Provide a “SIEM export validation” CLI command that sends a test event and checks connectivity + TLS certs.

4) Air-gapped scoring options
We need a clear scoring matrix for Private:
- Mode A (Full scoring): customer can run scoring workers (CPU/GPU) inside their environment.
  - Support eval-harness runner packaged for offline use (container image + pinned rubric bundle)
  - Model-graded evals allowed only if customer provides the grader model endpoint internally (no external network).
- Mode B (Heuristics only): no grader model allowed.
  - Provide built-in heuristic metrics: refusal rate (pattern-based), JSON/format adherence, tool-call shape checks, length/verbosity drift, blocked-token markers, etc.
  - Important: label these metrics as “heuristic” in Console to avoid misinterpretation.
- Mode C (Metrics-only): shadowing enabled but scoring disabled.
  - Still emit “shadow_target_success_rate”, “shadow_capture_rate”, “scoring_lag_seconds” (N/A), and basic latency/cost diffs; quality metrics omitted.

Out of scope
- Customer-uploaded arbitrary code execution inside Redwood Private (v1)
- Long-term offline replay of historical traffic beyond configured retention

Implementation plan (engineering)
A) Control plane / config
- Add Private-only config defaults in policy service for shadow traffic:
  - sampling_percent default 0
  - allow_payload_storage default false
  - retention defaults as above
- Validation changes:
  - If allow_payload_storage=false, reject configs that request “sampled examples” endpoints
  - If storage_backend=none, require scoring_mode != full (no payload refs to score)
  - Ensure redact_mode set for any payload persistence

B) Data plane / ingestion
- Ensure no dependency on Redwood-managed queues/storage for Private:
  - Support pluggable queue adapter: {kafka | sqs | pubsub | rabbitmq | local}
  - Backpressure/circuit breaker must short-circuit shadow path when queue unavailable (drop shadow; continue control)
- Confirm streaming behavior in Private: only capture final aggregated output by default; optionally capture chunks if allow_payload_storage=true and max_bytes configured.

C) Scoring subsystem
- Package rubric templates and prompt skeletons as versioned bundles that can be synced to Private installs.
- Make rubric_version required for full scoring; store it with aggregate results to prevent cross-rubric comparisons.
- Provide “air-gapped rubric update” procedure (documented steps + checksum verification).

D) SIEM export
- Extend audit log emitter (from ENG-5417) to support Private export sinks.
- Add minimal “shadow_traffic.*” event types:
  - shadow_experiment.created/updated/disabled
  - shadow_policy.applied/removed
  - shadow_scoring.worker_degraded (lag threshold exceeded)
  - shadow_redaction.config_changed

Acceptance criteria
- Private deployment can enable shadow traffic with sampling=0% default and explicit admin enablement required.
- Private deployment can run in three scoring modes (full / heuristics-only / metrics-only) without external network access.
- Retention defaults match policy; raw artifacts are OFF by default and never stored unless allow_payload_storage=true.
- SIEM export emits audit/ops events with zero prompt/response text; includes experiment_id and route_id.
- All failure modes are fail-open for user traffic (shadow drop only) and observable via dashboards/alerts.
- Docs: “Private considerations” section added to Shadow Traffic Quickstart with a decision tree for scoring modes.

Notes / open questions
- Do we require a separate RBAC permission for allow_payload_storage=true in Private (e.g., Security Admin)? Proposed: yes.
- Do we support local filesystem storage at all? Initial proposal: only for on-prem POC; not recommended for production.
- For metrics-only mode, do we still compute quality deltas from cached/previous scores? Proposal: no (avoid mixed semantics).

References
- Confluence: sources/confluence/security-and-compliance/data-residency-and-retention/shadow-traffic-data-retention-and-redaction.json
- Confluence: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/observability-standards/quality-metrics-observability-standard.json
- Linear: ENG-5411 (retention/redaction implementation), ENG-5417 (audit logs), ENG-5405 (scoring pipeline), ENG-5415 (backpressure/fail-open)

Rollout plan (Private)
- Feature-flag: shadow_traffic_private_enabled (default OFF)
- Internal Private test env first (dogfood), then 1–2 design partners with explicit retention approval.

Owner notes
- Kevin Osei: driving SIEM export + retention defaults alignment with audit/SIEM requirements.
- Marcus Lin / Naomi Feldman to review config/RBAC and confirm default OFF posture for payload persistence.

Risks
- Air-gapped rubric bundle updates become operationally heavy; mitigate with strict versioning and a stable v1 rubric set.
- SIEM export misconfiguration could become noisy; mitigate with rate limiting + “test event” tool + clear docs.
- Customers may expect model-graded metrics without providing internal grader model; mitigate with upfront UI copy + docs, and heuristics-only fallback.

2026-02-14 (Sean Gallagher): SRE ask: add a single dashboard tile for ‘shadow drop rate’ and ‘queue unavailable’ so Private operators can see fail-open behavior at a glance. Ensure alerting is ticket-only by default in Private.
